Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. historical_references.reference: The Mahabharata: A Translation. Penguin Books. 1996. Arjuna, also known as Arjuna the Invincible, is a central character in this epic Sanskrit poem. Arjuna is a warrior in the Kuru Kingdom, one of the two major factions in the great war of Kurukshetra. Arjuna is the great-nephew of Bhishma and the cousin of Bhima, Karna, and Duryodhana. Arjuna is also a disciple of the sage Dhaumya, and is married to Subhadra, the sister of Krishna.

Vedic Gods and Goddesses: An Illustrated Dictionary. Motilal Banarsidass. 1997. Arjuna is also known as Arjun, Arjith, or Arjitha. He is also referred to as Indrajit, the vanquisher of Indra. Arjuna is the third of the five sons of Indra, the god of rain, and the goddess Sachi. Arjuna was born from the eyes of Indra, when he was distracted from the battle against the demon Tripura.
